text:
Seattle visits Florida tonight with the results ahead of the chances. The Kraken have taken 47% of the expected goals at five on five, against 54% for the Panthers, and their +8 goal difference sits on -2.4 expected, propped up by finishing and goaltending. Florida creates 3.28 expected goals per 60 and allows 3.11, while Seattle sits at 3.10 and 3.39. The model projects 3.31 goals for Florida and 3.01 for Seattle. The Panthers will be missing Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, both on injured reserve, and the model accounts for that.

Special teams lean Florida's way. The Panthers generate 1.31 power-play expected goals a game against Seattle's 0.58, and they draw six penalties a game, though they also take 5.1, which keeps feeding opponents. In net, Seattle's projected starter Joey Daccord is +1.11 goals saved above expected this season after -6.1 last year in 47 games. Florida's projected goalie Akira Schmid is at -0.42 this season (.876) and -1.1 last year in 34 games. Neither has a strong record to lean on.

Seattle is 3-1-1 in its last five but had 47% of the expected goals in those games and won the chance battle once. Florida is 3-2-0 with 51%, ahead on chances in four of five. The Kraken close out a five-game road trip, 3-0-1 so far. Watch Matthew Tkachuk, on a seven-game point streak and 70% to record a point, and Sam Reinhart, 39% to score and the top power-play threat. For Seattle, Jared McCann is 30% to score, though he is flagged as due to cool.
